Reviewing the peer responses, all models—including my previous one—agree on the fundamental historical facts:
1. Marie Antoinette never uttered the phrase (disproving Option A). The phrase appears in Jean-Jacques Rousseau's *Confessions*, written around 1765 when Marie Antoinette was still a child in Austria.
2. Rousseau attributed the phrase to a "great princess" or "princess of the blood," and historians frequently suggest this may have referred to Maria Theresa of Spain, the wife of Louis XIV (supporting Option B).

There is no reason to change the conclusion, as the peer responses strongly corroborate the reasoning that Option (B) is the correct historical choice.

Final answer: B
